chunks: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Was God (existing) and there was nothing?' He said: 'Yes, He was and there was nothing.' I said: 'So where would He be?' He was reclining, then sat upright and said: 'You have asked the impossible, O Zurara, and you inquired about place when there was no place.'

key_terms.أحلت: You asked the impossible/incoherent — a philosophical term denoting a category error or logical impossibility
key_terms.إذ لا مكان: When there was no place — affirming that place itself is a contingent, created reality
key_terms.المكان: Place/location — a created spatial category that did not exist before creation

ai.seo_question: Where was God before creation according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Zurara ibn A'yan — one of the most trusted companions of Imam al-Baqir (AS) — poses a profound philosophical question about God's pre-eternal existence and location. The Imam's dramatic physical response (sitting upright from a reclining position) emphasizes the gravity of the answer: the question of God's 'place' before creation is logically impossible, because place itself is a created category. This is a foundational Shia theological statement on divine transcendence — God is not bound by spatial categories, which did not exist prior to creation. The word 'أَحَلْتَ' (you asked the impossible/incoherent) is a technical philosophical term indicating a category error.
